AUTHOR: Shah
TITLE: A Zero Shot Detection Based Approach for Fish Species Recognition in Underwater Environments
SPECIES: 51 SEAMAPD21 reef fish classes (44 seen / 7 unseen: Lutjanus campechanus, Pagrus pagrus, Rhomboplites aurorubens, Seriola dumerili, Pristipomoides aquilonaris, Epinephelus morio, Holacanthus bermudensis)
DATA: SEAMAPD21 (NOAA SEFSC video survey; 130 classes, 28,319 images; subset of 51 classes used)
V_EV: no statement found (only 'low-resolution nature of the images and the difficulty in distinguishing between fish and the background')
D2: Seen/unseen class split 44/7; image train/test split not reported
D_EV: no statement found (only class split: 'Out of 51 distinct fish species classes in SEAMAPD21, we use the seen/unseen split of 44/7.')
R_EV: Sec. III-B: 'The dataset used in this study is the Southeast Area Monitoring and Assessment Program Dataset 2021 (SEAMAPD21)' - single dataset; unseen classes are from the same dataset.
C_EV: no statement found (no confidence threshold reported; only IoU thresholds 0.4-0.7 for mAP)

ARCH: Faster R-CNN ResNet-101 + conditional WGAN feature synthesizer with triplet and cyclic-consistency losses (zero-shot detection)
METR: mAP and per-class AP at IoU 0.4-0.7 for seen and unseen classes
